newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries steady in London,look to Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady in London,look to Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady to marginally higher on Tuesday, dealers said, in the absence of key economic indicators later in the session.
"Greenspan is speaking, and anything he has to say about monetary policy will be the most important thing for today," said Rob Hayward, economic adviser at BankAmerica in London.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivers a speech sponsored by the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars at 0100 GMT/2100 EDT.
The Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond releases monthly manufacturing and services indices at 1400 GMT.
"That might attract some interest in the absence of anything else," said Hayward.
The long bond was trading at 97-16 at 0959 GMT, to yield 6.821 pct, unchanged from Tokyo and 1/32 above the New York close.
September T-bond futures were 3/32 higher at 110-22 in automated trade.
"We've seen a more volatile range of prices than recently," said Charles Quigley, vice president at Chase in London. "There's been some swap interest and some speculative demand."
There was nervousness about a further upswing in the market after many participants were caught out by Friday's short-covering rally following the release of May employment data, Quigley said.
"Most people want to take the view that the game is not over yet."
